summary: # Marvelous Designer 12.2 Tutorial: One-Shoulder Swimsuit ## Introduction Welcome to the Xieye Tutorial in Summer! This tutorial is designed to help beginners understand the basics of Marvelous Designer. In this session, we will learn how to make a one-shoulder swimsuit. ## Setting Up the Virtual Model First, insert your virtual model into the work area. Today, we will use Hana as our virtual model. You can insert her into the work area by navigating to **Library > Avatar > Hana**. ### Navigating the 3D Window In the default settings, hold down the mouse button and drag to rotate the view in the 3D window. Use the mouse wheel to zoom in or out. To temporarily close the window and make the work area larger, click the X in the upper right corner. ## Creating the Swimsuit We will create a basic version of the swimsuit. Go to the 2D toolbar to find the tool group for creating the garment. We want to select the multidirectional tool, which can be accessed using the shortcut key **H**. ### Drawing the Swimsuit Shape - Click the shortcut key to draw a straight line. - Click again to create a shape. - Press **Backspace** to return to the previous step. - Use **Ctrl** while clicking to draw a curve. - Press **Shift** to draw along the reference line. - Press **Esc** to recreate the entire shape. ### Drawing the Joint Swimsuit Start drawing from the neck point in the front: 1. Press **Ctrl** and click to draw the neck curve. 2. Click at a certain position above the shoulder to create the shoulder strap. 3. Follow the curve drawn by the shoulder to draw the shoulder line. 4. Press **Ctrl** to draw a curve below the leaf. 5. Draw outward when creating the curve below the leaf, saving the side amount. 6. Release the **Ctrl** key and click to draw a straight line, completing the rest of the line. Create a straight line as a stop point at the waist for subsequent adjustments. You can refer to the model's internal body style for guidance. ### Adjusting the Bottom Panel While creating the bottom panel, draw a longer part similar to the shoulder strap. Refer to the pink straight line to draw the bottom point in the front, then click on the starting point to complete the closed shape of the panel. ## Viewing the Panels Now, both the 3D and 2D windows will appear simultaneously. The panel displays a texture surface in the default situation, currently white. Switch to a fully transparent surface in the 2D display column to objectively see if any panel overlaps. ### Copying and Mirroring the Panel Select the full panel and right-click to choose **Mirror Paste**. This will create a front and back panel. The back panel and the front panel are similar, but adjustments will be needed. ## Editing the Panels To facilitate panel adjustments, click on the small scissors to access the edit panel tool group. Use the edit panel tool to adjust the point line and the panel shape: 1. In the front middle section, click the right button and select **Align to Open Edit Panel** to maintain the panel's alignment. 2. Use the adjustment panel tool for further refinement. ### Molding the Panel Lines The line molding tool is the most commonly used tool for merging lines. Pay attention to the direction of the panel line to ensure they correspond correctly. ## Finalizing the Swimsuit After creating the panel line, go to the 3D window and display the virtual model. Click the align button at the bottom to quickly place the panel around the model. The blue dots represent the alignment points. ### Creating the Lining Line Use the line marking tool to create the lining line, ensuring the direction is accurate. After simulating, you will adjust the clothing. Address any creases that appear, especially around the waist, since they might indicate fabric misalignment with the model's curves. ## Adjusting the Fit When adjusting the fabric around the waist, we can use the extension tool to modify the plate. Click the waist point that does not need modification, then move the mouse horizontally to adjust the back. ### Refining the Curves Use the edit curve tool to ensure the front and back curves connect smoothly without obvious angles. Adjust the elastic properties for the lower curve and neck curve to create a tighter fit. ## Final Adjustments Check the side view to ensure the side seam line is straight. Move the neck point to adjust the depth of the opening, smoothing out any curve irregularities. Adjust the shoulder strap at the back to enhance the swimsuit's appearance. ### Adding Design Elements Once the basic swimsuit is complete, we can add additional design features. Change the model's hairstyle by clicking the reset button in the lower right corner. Navigate to the **Elegant Stylized Hair** folder for options. ## Optimizing the Design Use the originator curve tool to enhance the waistline's curvature. Adjust the front and back pieces, applying changes as necessary. ### Creating Asymmetric Designs For asymmetric designs and color division, create reference lines on the board. Remove the symmetrical relationship by selecting the front and back boards and using the adjustment board tool. ### Cutting and Applying Fabrics Select the cut line on the front and back boards, then proceed to cut the board. After cutting, remember to reapply elasticity to the lines. ## Finalizing Fabric and Textures We will use multiple types of fabrics for texture. Go to the **Substance** file in the library window and drag the desired materials onto the swimsuit. Adjust the color and properties in the property editor as needed. ### Simulation and Export After adjusting the particle diameter for better fold details, open the simulation application to see the final result. You can then export the project for rendering in other 3D software. ## Conclusion Thank you for watching this tutorial on creating a one-shoulder swimsuit in Marvelous Designer 12.2. Be sure to check out other tutorials in the Summer Atmosphere Series for more design ideas!
